problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 2 \\ -6 & 7 & 1 \\ -7 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 1 \\ -11 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -7 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
feedback.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-9{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -7 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-9{C}_{1}.$
